body:
## Resolves 

- https://github.com/elastic/security-team/issues/12681
- https://github.com/elastic/security-team/issues/12682

## Summary

Please find the summary of all the changes below.

### Last Execution Info

This Enhancement introduces `last_execution` object to the `migration` document. There is some information that we need to add for the last run migration ( eg. `error` occured or `connector_id` used ). This PR add that info. Below is how a sample `migration` document looks like with `last_execution` info and shape of `last_execution` object.

```ts
export const RuleMigrationLastExecution = z.object({
  /**
   * The moment the last execution started.
   */
  started_at: z.string().optional(),
  /**
   * The moment the last execution ended.
   */
  ended_at: z.string().optional(),
  /**
   * The connector ID used for the last execution, if applicable.
   */
  connector_id: z.string().optional(),
  /**
   * The error message if the last execution failed.
   */
  error: z.string().optional(),
  /**
   * Indicates if the last execution was aborted by the user.
   */
  is_aborted: z.boolean().optional(),
});
```
```json
{
  "created_by": "u_v6jVi3qZ21kAEUwmbl-sfujRnwydrltycxyByl3jtIM_0",
  "created_at": "2025-05-28T06:10:37.638Z",
  "last_execution": {
    "connector_id": "azureOpenAiGPT4o",
    "started_at": "2025-05-28T06:10:48.030Z",
    "is_aborted": false,
    "error": "Failed to populate ELSER indices. Make sure the ELSER model is deployed and running at Machine Learning > Trained Models. Error: Exception when running inference id [.elser-2-elasticsearch] on field [elser_embedding]",
    "ended_at": "2025-05-28T06:11:31.464Z"
}

```

### Why `Last Execution` info was needed?



- An automatic migration can run into an error and terminate. Today, we store that error in server state and do not persist. This can be a problem when server is restarted and user will not be able to see that error.
  - So, we need a way to persist the error for last execution.
- Additionally, we do not have any details on when the last execution was started and finished.

- We also need to store the connector_id so that we can re-use it when user is restarting a migration.


In addition to resolving above issues, this Ticket makes some minor UI Changes to the Migration Ready Panel in different states of a Migration


### When Migration is Ready to be started.

Original description:

> The `test_cutless_checkbox.py` file on the `MessageBroker` branch is failing its first scenario:
> 
> - Scenario 1 (`test_scenario_1_bad_url`) starts the app with `--cutless` and supplies an invalid DizqueTV URL.
> - After calling `LogicController.check_dizquetv_compatibility()`, the test expects the Cutless checkbox to be hidden (`cutless_checkbox_visible == False`). Instead, the checkbox remains visible because the `cutless` flag is never reset to `False` when the compatibility check fails.
> 
> To fix this, we need to update `GUI/FlagManager.py` in the `evaluate_platform_compatibility` method:
> 
> 1. When handling `platform_type == 'dizquetv'` and a `platform_url` is provided:
>    - Call `cls._check_dizquetv_advanced(platform_url)` to determine compatibility.
>    - If `compatible` is `True`, call `cls.set_cutless(True)` and return `True`.
>    - If `compatible` is `False`, call `cls.set_cutless(False)`, print a status message, and return `False`.
> 2. Add an `elif platform_type == 'dizquetv'` branch (with no URL) to also disable cutless.
> 3. Ensure that callers (in `GUI/FrontEndLogic.py` methods like `save` or `on_continue_button_click`) synchronize `LogicController.cutless` and broadcast updates by reading from `FlagManager.cutless` after evaluation.
> 
> Once this change is merged, running `pytest test_cutless_checkbox.py` should pass all three scenarios, and the Cutless checkbox visibility logic will behave correctly.

author: reductionista
body:
JIRA: [PLEX-1453](https://smartcontract-it.atlassian.net/browse/PLEX-1453)

#Description 

The specific error on hyperliquid we need to handle is "invalid block range", but the general error condition it represents is a state where the rpc server is permanently missing one or more blocks requested in an eth_getLogs range request.

This is required for hyperliquid, but could also be useful for any rpc server which prunes logs or blocks. If they've been permanently pruned, we want to continue. Adding for hyperlqiuid now, but making it configurable will make it easy to add support for any other chains we see this issue come up on.  Both immediately for the short term (via a custom toml config regex) and for the longer term by adding another regex to this `MissingBlocks` error & appropriate error code.

[PLEX-1453]: https://smartcontract-it.atlassian.net/browse/PLEX-1453?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

## Summary
- Fix jest command not found error in test coverage CI job
- Fix lint command mismatch in CI/CD pipeline workflow
- Fix E2E test helper to properly skip tests when Docker images are missing

## Details

### Issues Fixed:
1. **Test Coverage Job**: Changed `jest` to `npx jest` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to fix "command not found" error
2. **CI/CD Pipeline**: Changed `npm run lint` to `npm run lint:check` in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to match package.json scripts
3. **E2E Test Failures**: Fixed `conditionalDescribe` function in `test/e2e/utils/testHelpers.js` to properly skip tests when required Docker images are missing

### Root Causes:
- CI pipeline was calling `jest` directly instead of via npm/npx
- Workflow was using wrong lint script name 
- E2E tests were failing with exit code 125 when Docker images weren't available instead of skipping gracefully

## 概要

Issue #36 の実装として、Slackページの709行におよぶ巨大なコンポーネントを複数の小さなコンポーネントに分離し、保守性と可読性を大幅に向上させました。

## 変更内容

### 新規作成コンポーネント
- **SlackHeroSection**: ヒーロー・説明セクション (約100行)
- **SlackSearchForm**: メイン検索フォーム (約180行)  
- **SlackAdvancedFilters**: 詳細フィルター条件 (約80行)

### 新規作成フック・ユーティリティ
- **useSlackSearch**: 検索ロジックの抽出 (約200行)
- **slackUtils.tsx**: ユーティリティ関数群 (約100行)

### リファクタリング効果
- **分離前**: 709行の巨大なSlackページコンポーネント
- **分離後**: 130行のシンプルなページコンポーネント + 複数の専門化されたコンポーネント

- TypeScript型安全性を完全維持
- プロップドリリングを最小化したClean Architecture

body:
## Description of change

Adds logic in our s3 service layer for the `delete_files` endpoint (ensuring status codes are passed up to endpoint level).
Unit tests and Postman tests have been added/updated accordingly.


If successful, a 200 204 (success, no content) success code is returned

If unsuccessful, we return:
- at router level
    - 400 bad request (e.g. no file specified)
    - 403 forbidden (e.g. incorrect permissions)
- at s3_service level (surfaced in the `outcomes` dict returned at the router level)
    - 404 file not found (e.g. file not found in specified bucket)
    - 500 generic error

#### Reference Issues/PRs
Fixes #4045

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.
This PR updates and completes the docstrings for the `VAR` class in the forecasting module.  
Specifically, it adds detailed explanations for the parameters:
- `method`: Specifies the estimation method, e.g., "ols" (ordinary least squares) or "mle" (maximum likelihood).
- `freq`: Defines the expected frequency of the input time series, e.g., "D" for daily, "M" for monthly.
- `dates`: Clarifies the expected date formats or types that can be passed.
- `missing`: Describes how missing data is handled, with valid options such as "none", "drop", or "raise".

These additions improve usability and reduce confusion for users implementing VAR forecasting.

#### Does your contribution introduce a new dependency? If yes, which one?
No.

#### What should a reviewer concentrate their feedback on?
- Accuracy and clarity of the parameter descriptions.
- Consistency with existing documentation style.
- Any missing information that could help users better understand the VAR class.

No new tests were added as this change only updates documentation.

author: gamenot
body:
Previous implementation selected target objects from only the last sub-scene (-1) causing scene cross-contamination if information from `target_object` was used. Original RL behavior after implementing the rewards generally resulted in reaching to a constant location on parallel environments due to referencing objects from a single scene.

Improvements:
- Use the batched RNG which scales already by `num_envs`.
- Generate the RNG for target selection only once for all sub-scenes.
- Select the target object for each sub-scene (i) from each sub-scene (i).

author: quick-flash
body:
This should speedup some of the RC filtering updating. Instead of needing to redundantly calculate the same cutoff and pt3 filter k for 3 difference filters on each axis (9 times) we can instead just calculate the pt3 filter k value once and then apply that k to each filter, saving many calculations. I have also reduced the amount of checks for if initialized. Now feedforward cutoff and setpoint cutoff are always the same (was already the same in 95+% of setups anyhow).

Also fix the issue where the feedforward_smooth_factor would be dependent on the rx rate (ie the filter cutoff would change based on the looprate).

Bonus points, I added faster ptxFilterGainFromDelay functions, so now if you ever want to calculate a filter using a tau instead of a cutoff and update it on the fly it'll be faster to run than it was previously.

body:
This PR introduces optional configuration caching to avoid or reduce repeated execution of default functions, which can have a high costs in form of API requests etc.

The caching will be per default disabled to remain the current behaviour and needs to be enabled and configured in the applications. Enabling caching has to happen initially when creating a config with `WithCachingEnabled()` but can be adapted at runtime since the configuration values are also available as configuration values themselves.

Within this PR I added some small helpers like `toBool()` and `toDuration()`

body:
<!--
Thanks for your contribution. Please make sure to fill the contents of this template with the necessary information to ease and speed up the review process.

!!! PLEASE DO NOT DELETE ANY SECTION, COMMENT OR THE CONTENT OF THE TEMPLATE. !!!
-->

### Summary of the Pull Request
Detects the use of the `syslog` syscall with action code 5 (SYSLOG_ACTION_CLEAR),
(4 is SYSLOG_ACTION_READ_CLEAR and 6 is SYSLOG_ACTION_CONSOLE_OFF) which clears the kernel
ring buffer (dmesg logs). This can be used by attackers to hide traces after exploitation
or privilege escalation. A common technique is running `dmesg -c`, which triggers this syscall internally.
 pls note :‌ we must add :
 -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S syslog -F a0=4 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S syslog -F a0=5 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S syslog -F a0=6 -k disable_dmesg_logs

 -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S syslog -F a0=4 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S syslog -F a0=5 -k clear_dmesg_logs
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S syslog -F a0=6 -k disable_dmesg_logs

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2458ab9-183b-4847-ab55-955a52166051)


### Example Log Event
```JSON
{
  "type": "SYSCALL",
  "msg": "audit(1748292286.470:6928)",
  "arch": "c000003e",

author: bossjones
body:
## Summary
- Add comprehensive YouTube download support with API and CLI fallback strategies
- Create enhanced AI-assisted development documentation and custom Claude Code commands
- Implement comprehensive test coverage for YouTube functionality
- Add development tooling and workflow automation

## Key Features

### YouTube Download Support
- **YouTubeDownloadStrategy**: Full implementation with API-first approach and CLI fallback
- **Quality Selection**: Support for 720p, 1080p, and audio-only downloads
- **Metadata Extraction**: Complete video metadata including duration, views, likes, upload date
- **Error Handling**: Robust error handling with graceful fallbacks between API and CLI modes

### Development Documentation
- **AI Documentation**: Portable `ai_docs/red/README.md` for Red-DiscordBot patterns (adaptable to other projects)
- **Claude Code Commands**: Custom slash commands for enhanced AI-assisted development:
  - `/context_prime` - Basic project context establishment
  - `/context_prime_w_lead` - Enhanced context with specific file reading
  - `/jprompt_ultra_diff_review` - Multi-LLM code review workflow
  - `/tdd_dpytest` - Comprehensive TDD workflow for Discord bot development
  - `/write_dpytest` - Quick dpytest test generation tool
- **Development Guide**: Complete documentation at `docs/development/claude_code/README.md`

### Test Coverage
- **Comprehensive YouTube Tests**: 100% coverage of YouTube strategy functionality
- **Quality Selection Tests**: Validation of video quality and audio-only download options
- **Error Scenario Testing**: API failures, network issues, and edge cases
- **Mock Integration**: Proper mocking of external APIs and CLI tools

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- Follows established strategy pattern from Twitter and Reddit implementations
- Implements `BaseDownloadHandler` interface for consistent platform handling
- Uses feature flags for API/CLI mode selection with fallback capabilities

### Integration Points
- **Discord Bot**: Full integration with downloads cog
- **CLI Interface**: Command-line access via boss-bot CLI
- **Test Framework**: dpytest integration for Discord bot testing
- **Quality Standards**: Passes all linting, type checking, and test requirements

## Test Plan
- [x] Unit tests for YouTube strategy (API and CLI modes)
- [x] Integration tests with Discord bot commands
- [x] Error handling and edge case validation
- [x] Quality selection and audio-only download testing
- [x] Mock accuracy verification for external dependencies

author: eatprilosec
body:
both the RG351MP and R35S ArkOS u-boots seem to load `rg351mp-kernel.dtb`, but when compiled, this u-boot looks for and loads `rk3326-rg351mp-linux.dtb`, which is also included with arkOS, notably redefining the gpio pin for download mode, and forces the device into Rockchip's download mode.

this rectifies the situation making this u-boot conform to arkOS's current boot process, allowing the device to boot arkOS

I'm guessing this change got lost at some point while adding support for RG351MP or the different panels and was never committed.

author: ruben-lohberg
body:
- Add "spreadsheetID" as an argument of getSheetID
- Add appropriate spreadsheet IDs to all calls of function getSheetID

Hintergrund:
Ich brauche für meinen Meldungen-Bot die funktion "Copy Sheet", welche intern "getSheetID" aufruft. Copy sheet hat eine "spreadsheetID" als parameter genommen, aber intern dann "getSheetID" immer hart mit "process.env.SPREADSHEET_ID_MASTERDATA" aufgerufen. 

Das war auf jeden fall falsch, da die funktion getSheetID in general/sheet.js liegt, nicht etwa in general/masterdata/sheet.js oder arbeitsstunden/sheet.js wo immer das Masterdata sheet genommen wird.

Die anderen Funktionen in  general/sheet.js nehmen alle eine spreadsheetID seit [!60](https://github.com/Roy0815/slack-service-bot/pull/60). Die funktion getSheetID ist mir damals wohl durch die Lappen gegangen (mea culpa).

In meinen Meldungen branch habe ich das bereits gemerged, da tut es.

author: copilot
body:
## Issue
The `SendAsync_CanBeCanceled_SendAsyncCancel` test in `SmtpClientTest` was failing in CI because it was using `Assert.IsType<OperationCanceledException>` to verify exception types. This assertion was too strict as it only passes when the exact type is matched, not when derived types like `TaskCanceledException` are thrown.

## Fix
Changed the assertion from:
```csharp
Assert.IsType<OperationCanceledException>(e.Error.InnerException);
```

To:
```csharp
Assert.IsAssignableFrom<OperationCanceledException>(e.Error.InnerException);
```

This allows the test to pass when the inner exception is of type `OperationCanceledException` or any derived type (like `TaskCanceledException`), which matches the actual behavior of the cancellation system.

Fixes #116041.

author: jackdiodati
body:
Added an additional parameter in the fene bond code.  This parameter controls whether or not lammps will allow fene bonds to extend past the set max bond length r0 (r_max).  Currently lammps allows fene bonds to extend to twice the length of the fixed max bond length, which is quite nonphysical but allowable for simulations where the bonds are not stretched much.  For simulations involving stretching bonds, this causes the simulation results to be invalid.  Thank you for your time

author: dnlbui
body:
**Summary of Changes:**

- **Contact Toll Data Structure:**
  - Added `toll`, `tollRequiredToSend`, and `tollRequiredToReceive` fields to each contact in localStorage.
  - `toll` is a BigInt representing the toll amount for sending messages.
  - `tollRequiredToSend` and `tollRequiredToReceive` indicate whether a toll is required (0: none, 1: required, 2: blocking).

- **Chat Modal Logic:**
  - When opening a chat, the app now:
    - Calls `updateTollValue(address)` to update the toll value in the background.
    - Calls the new `updateContactToll(address)` function to synchronize toll requirements from the network and update the local contact object.
  - `updateContactToll(address)`:
    - Fetches the latest toll requirements for both sender and receiver from the network.
    - Updates the local contact object if the network values differ from localStorage.

- **Documentation:**
  - Added detailed comments explaining the new toll fields and the logic for updating them.

… the implementation

To ease the review process, please consider the following before opening a pull request:
- [ ] the code is sufficiently well documented (e.g. inline comments)
- [ ] the relevant README(s) were updated. See e.g. https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/main/detector/calorimeter/README.md or https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/main/FCCee/IDEA/compact/README.md
- [ ] the code is covered by tests. See https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/blob/main/test/CMakeLists.txt
- [ ] the PR source branch has been rebased (`--ff-only`) to `k4geo/main`
- [ ] the PR does not contain any additions or modifications that do not belong to it
- [ ] The release notes below contain a succinct and comprehensive description of the changes that are sufficiently self-explanatory

If you are modifying detector dimensions or adding new xml parameters, also consider the following:
- [ ] the xml file free parameters that can not be modified without additional prescriptions are well indicated
- [ ] the changes in this PR have not introduced any overlaps. You can check so with the following command: `ddsim --compactFile PATH_TO_COMPACT_FILE --runType run --ui.commandsInitialize "/geometry/test/run" > overlapDump.txt`

BEGINRELEASENOTES
Add a straw tube tracker for ALLEGRO concept.  The implementation was discussed at the FCC Full Sim Meeting on May 28: https://indico.cern.ch/event/1551837/#71-straw-tube-tracker-implemen.  This discussion included the memory load of the straw concept, which is on the order of 200MB.  The logical volume count is minimized by sharing logical tube volumes for each multilayer, however due to the use of cylindrical tube geometry the number of faces is large.

The straw tracker concept uses thin-wall straws (12um) to achieve high spatial resolution.  The main possible advantage over a drift chamber concept is a modular construction with each readout channel corresponding to a single unit.  Additionally, because each tube is a single unit there are no B field correction factors needed to compute spatial position, and it is expected that the straws may achieve a slightly higher single hit position resolution compared to a drift chamber.

Changes:
 - Create new ALLEGRO version o2_v01 with straw tracker
 - Corresponding READMEs in ALLEGRO and detector/tracker
 - Straw tracker C++ implementation in detector/tracker folder
 - Uses same dimensions as drift chamber for easy interchange of the two tracker concepts
 - Both .xml and .cpp code for straw tracker have readable, useful comments
 - For ALLEGRO_o2_v01 ONLY (the straw tube implementation), extend the silicon wrapper z extent to +/-3m to make full use of the available space
 - Default straw tracker implementation has +/-2 degree stereo angle alternating for even/odd multilayers
 - Straw tracker tube size matches IDEA for innermost cells (8mm) and increases linearly with radial distance (saturating at 2.5cm diameter tubes) from interaction point to minimize total N tubes, which minimizes multiple scattering and improves resolution.

ENDRELEASENOTES

author: drappier-charles
body:
# Goal 
Our standard user have only one agent in one repo, or even a mono repo with multiple agent, but independent
like this
```
myagent1/
|-blaxel.toml
|-...
myagent2/
|-Dockerfile
|-blaxel.toml 
|-...
```
With that, he can easily do thing like that

```
cd myagent1 && bl deploy
cd myagent2 && bl deploy
```

Goal is to handle another use case
```
myagent1/
|-blaxel.toml
|-...
myagent2/
|-Dockerfile
|-blaxel.toml 
|-...
shared/
|-shared.ts
```

If we keep same command, shared will not be send during build phase and it will failed

The current PR allow to do that
`bl deploy -f myagent1`
`bl deploy -f myagent2`

What does it mean
-> It mean than the whole folder is send at each build, we bulk everything, and we build with a Dockerfile and a blaxel.toml in the path define through -f

# Why this command line :
It was inspired by some other library like docker

`docker build -t myimage .`
The . refer to local path as context

`docker build -f subfolder/Dockerfile -t myimage .`
Here the path is still the current folder, but Dockerfile is taken in a subfolder, so it allow with same context to build multiple image, similar to our use case


# Important
This is working only with typescript right now, goal is to define if we keep that this way, and do python and cleaning after


Dockerfile need to start with root context, not the folder (requirement with docker)
I think we may want to automate the standard dockerfile to handle it, right now it require a custom one

## Exemple of Dockerfile with my example
```
...
COPY agent1/src . (and not src)
COPY shared shared
...
```

body:
This fixes two issues:
- If all addons take less than 5 seconds to load, all minimap buttons were visible for a few seconds.
- If some addons take more than 5 seconds to load, their minimap button might not be "gathered".

`PLAYER_LOGIN` is called after all plugins were loaded, just before loading the world.
`PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` was also an option, but is called whenever changing zone, not just once.

I kept the 5-seconds timer, because some addons seem to load their minimap icon _after_ `PLAYER_LOGIN`, like `SuperAPI`.
I also added the `alreadyGathered` variable to keep track of which minimap icon was already gathered to not handle them twice.

author: jmcphers
body:
Prior to this change, each plot maintained its own render queue, with the result that when multiple plots were emitted, they would all try to render at once, resulting in timeouts. This change serializes all of the plot rendering work per session, so that:

- Render requests are not sent to the session until the session is idle. 
- Only one render request is sent at a time. 

Addresses https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/5954. 

Some dev notes:

- The reason things worked as they did in the past is that we didn't want to presume that a render would be handled on the main thread (perhaps some plots or some languages could render plots in the background). However, practically speaking this is the case for both our R and Python kernels. If we want to get maximum performance from backends that can do background rendering, we'll have to unwind some parts of this change and/or make it possible for the runtime to declare whether it can handle parallel or background plot rendering.
- This is a targeted change for plot comms, but practically speaking almost every comm could benefit from a task queue/serializer so that RPCs are executed in order and do not overlap with each other or with RPCs from other comms connected to the same runtime. We may want to consider making this a generic part of the comm infrastructure when we have the capacity for more risk.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Fix timeouts when rendering plots during slow-running operations or in a loop (#5954)

### QA Notes

The behavior is better for R than Python, since R sends a pre-render of each plot while code is running. For Python, you can expect that you'll have to wait to see the plot until the session is idle. This work is tracked in #7451. 

Test tags: `@:plots`

author: damianfarina
body:
## Summary

COMMAN users have no unified, reliable way to record, track, and fulfill client orders. This makes it hard to coordinate workflows, keep promises to clients, and clearly know what needs to be delivered or produced next. We need a simple, consistent flow for handling the entire sales order lifecycle.

## Solution

- Sales orders progress through a series of statuses: **quote**, **confirmed**, **fulfilled**, or **cancelled**.
- **While an order is still a quote:**
  - Users can freely add or remove products.
  - Product prices and client discounts are always up-to-date, reflecting any changes in the system.
- **When a quote is confirmed:**
  - The confirmation date is recorded.
  - Discounts and prices are finalized and stored as part of the order.
  - No further edits are allowed to products, prices, or discounts on the order.
  - Each product in the order begins the fulfillment process.
- **After confirmation:**
  - Each product can be manually updated to show its progress (e.g., ready for delivery, delivered, or cancelled).
  - An order is considered fulfilled once every product has either been delivered or cancelled. The fulfillment date is recorded.
  - After fulfillment, the order becomes read-only, except for adding comments or notes for future reference.

- This workflow supports partial fulfillment, real-time progress tracking, and ensures all important decisions are locked in at the moment of confirmation.

## Rabbit Holes to Avoid

- Do not attempt to automate purchasing, manufacturing, or supplier workflows in this cycle—simply track fulfillment at the product level.
- Skip historical revisions, complex reporting, taxes, invoicing, or client-facing features for now.
- Avoid over-complicating permissions and notifications; keep workflows simple and internal.

## No-Gos

- No integration with external systems.
- No returns, refunds, or post-fulfillment edits to orders (beyond comments/notes).
- No workflow for re-opening or reversing a fulfilled or cancelled order.

## Risks/Questions

- Users must clearly understand the meaning of each status and the consequences of confirmation (locked prices, no further edits).
- If a product becomes unavailable after order confirmation, users need guidance on next steps.
- Ensure there is a basic audit trail or log of status changes for future expansion.

author: ih-codes
body: ## :scroll: Tickets [Jira ticket](https://mozilla-hub.atlassian.net/browse/FXIOS-12331) [GitHub ticket](https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/firefox-ios/issues/26856) ## :bulb: Description ## Background Context Currently, when we add a new metrics.yaml file to our iOS project, we have to also make sure the [probe-scraper](https://github.com/mozilla/probe-scraper) repo is updated with a matching PR that adds (or updates) the relevant file paths (e.g. https://github.com/mozilla/probe-scraper/pull/902). Desktop has a bot that automatically picks up changes like this and creates a PR for the probe-scraper repo. We are hoping to do this for iOS as well so we can begin separating out our monolithic metrics.yaml file into smaller feature-specific YAML files. In order for this to work, Firefox for iOS needs a file which itemizes all our Glean YAMLs for consumption by a probe-scraper GitHub action ([additional context in ticket comments](https://mozilla-hub.atlassian.net/browse/FXIOS-12331?focusedCommentId=1071267)). ## Work in PR This PR adds a few important files: - **glean_index.yaml**: This will be the index of Glean files for the probe-scraper to leverage for generating automatic PRs - **gleanProbes.xcfilelist**: This is a generated file which inputs all our individual metric YAML files into the Xcode Client's "Glean SDK Generator Script" build phase - **FirefoxTelemetryUtility.sh**: This script helps developers add new feature metrics YAML files and automates updating file path references (i.e. updates the 2 above files with the new YAML file's path) The SDK Generator script was also updated. This script calls the Glean parser to convert our metrics YAML specifications into Swift code. The script now accepts input file lists as well as single input files, which lets us automate adding additional YAML dependencies for the build phase via `FirefoxTelemetryUtility.sh`. ## Testing Notes To run the new FirefoxTelemetryUtility shell script, navigate to the firefox-ios root directory and run the following command to manually update the glean index and glean probes file list: ``` ./FirefoxTelemetryUtility.sh --update ``` You would manually update if you've created a glean file, e.g. `settings.yaml` with probes manually, and want to automatically update the file paths in the `glean_index.yaml` and the xcode build phase input file list `gleanProbes.xcfilelist`. To test adding a new metrics YAML file, you can run the following: ``` ./FirefoxTelemetryUtility.sh --add AppIcon ``` ...where "AppIcon" is the example of a new feature or component for which we are adding new probes. You will see a corresponding `app_icon.yaml` file created in the `Client/Glean/probes` subdirectory, and this file path will also be automatically appended to the glean index file and the glean probes file list (same as the `--update` option). At this point, you should be able to build in Xcode and see your new probes. As well, the Xcode Glean folder will automatically update to reflect the new content in the `probes` subdirectory. ## Coming Soon I will be updating the README and the Wiki with details on script usage once this work is finalized. ## :pencil: Checklist - [x] I filled in the ticket numbers and a description of my work - [x] I updated the PR name to follow our [PR naming guidelines](https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/firefox-ios/wiki/Pull-Request-Naming-Guide) - [x] I ensured unit tests pass and wrote tests for new code - [ ] If working on UI, I checked and implemented accessibility (Dynamic Text and VoiceOver) - [ ] If adding telemetry, I read the [data stewardship requirements](https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/firefox-ios/wiki/Adding-Glean-Telemetry-Events) and will request a data review - [x] If needed, I updated documentation and added comments to complex code - [ ] If needed, I added a backport comment (example `@Mergifyio backport release/v120`)

author: jcjones
body:
As described in Issue #60, this PR removes the duplication of ACME Directory information from the issuer's Entity Configuration, favoring instead the URL to the ACME Directory as defined in RFC 8555.

Doing this removes the ability to identify changes in the ACME Directory information via the Entity Configuration, in exchange for simplification across the stack for clients and issuers. It's still possible to identify changes via the Directory directly. 

A point-by-point analysis of the consequences of this change is posted in https://github.com/peppelinux/draft-demarco-acme-openid-federation/issues/60#issuecomment-2688694461. Further commentary is welcome.

@peppelinux @selfissued

Fixes #60.
